item.title: A natural depsipeptide antibiotic binds the E-site of the bacterial ribosome
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10589-2

Improved fractionation strategies can identify antibiotics with previously unseen scaffolds and mechanisms, exemplified by manikomycin from Streptomyces rimosus, which acts by targeting the E-site of the bacterial large ribosomal subunit.

item.title: Earth’s east–west albedo symmetry
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10624-2

Analysis of a 25-year satellite record shows that Earth has a persistent east–west albedo symmetry split at 27° E, with clear-sky albedo, cloud radiative effect and open-ocean fraction exhibiting a triple symmetry around this meridian.

item.title: Relativistic electron acceleration at the bow shock of Jupiter and beyond
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10473-z

NASA’s Juno observations show relativistic electron acceleration at the bow shock of Jupiter and establish a universal scaling law linking shock size to maximum cosmic ray energy.

item.title: Acquired genetic and cell-state changes in IDH-mutant glioma progression
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10612-6

Longitudinal transcriptomic, chromatin and genomic analyses of the two types of IDH-mutant glioma reveal in detail how disease progression is influenced by interdependent genetic, epigenetic and microenvironmental factors.

item.title: Mining triggers extensive additional deforestation in sub-Saharan Africa
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10551-2

Extensive mining activity leads to large-scale deforestation of dense tropical forests across sub-Saharan Africa, driven particularly by key energy transition minerals such as cobalt.

item.title: Cold-induced peptide signalling secures pollen resilience and crop yield
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10603-7

A small-peptide signalling axis involving RGF family members controls resilience to cold stress in tomatoes and rice; modulating this pathway prevents cold-induced yield losses.

item.title: Teosinte alleles enhance nitrogen assimilation and seed protein in maize
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10575-8

Teosinte alleles enhance nitrogen assimilation and seed protein without lowering crop yield when expressed in modern maize, providing a powerful strategy for crop improvement to meet future population demands.

item.title: Cell-type-resolved genetic variation shapes inflammatory bowel disease risk
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10627-z

Single-cell mapping of cis-expression quantitative trait loci in inflammatory bowel disease revealed distal, enhancer-enriched variants detected at the cell-type level more frequently co-localize with genome-wide association study loci than those identified at the tissue level.

item.title: Plastoglobules compartmentalize nitrogen assimilation in maize
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10610-8

Chloroplast plastoglobules act as nitrogen-assimilation hubs in maize, with key enzymes enhancing nitrogen-use efficiency and offering new strategies for developing high-yield, sustainable crops.

item.title: Analysis of trade-offs of post-sorting plastic packaging
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10606-4

An analysis of post-sorting plastic packaging shows that target polymer purity is similar across source-separation and post-sorting pathways, but post-sorted plastics contain more contaminants that need to be removed before recyclate production.

item.title: Spermine is an endogenous iron chelator that inhibits ferroptosis
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10597-2

A non-canonical metabolic route for spermine synthesis mediated by ALDH18A1 limits iron availability and lipid peroxidation in hepatocellular carcinoma.

item.title: Chiral superfluorescence from perovskite superlattices at room temperature
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10637-x

Chiral perovskite superlattices exhibit room-temperature circularly polarized superfluorescence, with emission intensity and polarization controllable by weak magnetic fields.

item.title: Mechanophore cross-linking enhances ballistic energy dissipation of polymers
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10557-w

Embedding a small fraction of force-sensitive mechanophores as cross-links into common polymers enhances ballistic energy dissipation.

item.title: Commensal-derived acetylcholine enhances mucosal immune education
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10592-7

A diet–microbiome–host axis strengthens mucosal immune defences and reinforces host–microbiota mutualism.

item.title: Nuclear shell structure governs short-range nucleon pairing
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10616-2

The scattering of high-energy electrons from three different nuclei demonstrated that short-range-correlated pairing depends far more on the specific quantum orbitals occupied by nucleons than predicted by theoretical models.

item.title: High-pulse-energy integrated mode-locked laser using a Mamyshev oscillator
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10517-4

A Mamyshev oscillator mode-locked laser compactly integrated on a photonic-chip delivers nanojoule, femtosecond pulses.

item.title: LASER couples damage sensing to ESCRT assembly for lysosome repair
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10604-6

ATG8 conjugation on damaged lysosomes triggers rapid assembly of a protein complex containing TFG, which directs lysosomal membrane repair by recruiting ESCRT proteins to sites of damage.

item.title: Cooperation conflicts with equality when allocating public goods
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10550-3

Uniform sharing of public goods can boost cooperation in social networks, but often concentrates benefits among well-connected individuals, creating inequality despite greater collective success.

item.title: Enamel nanocrystal misorientation increased with meat-eating and agriculture
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10583-8

An analysis of enamel nanocrystal misorientation in primate and human teeth across three major dietary shifts in human evolution shows that misorientation increased with harder diets, suggesting that misorientation contributes to enamel’s resilience.

item.title: High-fidelity modular skeletons authenticate a Cambrian origin for Bryozoa
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10590-9

Exquisite early Cambrian fossils of Protomelission gatehousei and Dayingomelission hexaclitia preserve soft-tissue anatomy and skeletal microstructure, confirming that these taxa are definitively bryozoans and indicating a deeper origin for the Bryozoa than was first apparent.

item.title: Centromeric footprints preserve telomere integrity in ALT cancers
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10598-1

Centromeric DNA repeat insertions and CENP-A chromatin assembly are identified as genomic signatures that preserve telomere integrity in ALT cancer cells.

item.title: Queen cell architecture shapes honey bee queen development
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10534-3

Worker bee construction behaviour actively engineers a physicochemical niche that is crucial for queen development in honey bees.

item.title: Recovery of plastic from mixed waste boosts recycling rates but affects quality
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-01759-3

Recovering plastic packaging from mixed domestic waste, as well as collecting plastic waste already sorted by households, increases recycling volumes but raises contamination and safety risks. Policies that support the sorting of plastics from mixed waste at central facilities should have strict quality standards and investment in advanced purification systems to ensure safe recycling outcomes.

item.title: Jupiter observations reveal a simple scaling law for particle acceleration
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-01412-z

Supersonic shocks in the vicinity of Jupiter suggest that transient plasma structures could govern the acceleration of particles travelling through space.

item.title: How a rush for minerals is causing deforestation in tropical regions
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-01582-w

An analysis of the extent to which mining caused deforestation between 2001 and 2020 in areas near mines in sub-Saharan Africa could help conservation efforts.

item.title: A maize gene that coordinates flowering aids drought resistance
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-01745-9

The synchronous flowering of male and female flower clusters in maize is crucial, but drought disrupts this synchrony, leading to considerable yield losses. A gene called SAUR72 is shown to preserve flowering synchrony in drought conditions, offering a potential strategy for breeding drought-resilient maize varieties.

item.title: What a royal bedchamber provides the queen bee
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-01580-y

When considering what shapes animal development, factors such as genetics come to mind. For a queen bee, however, her special wax home also has a role.

item.title: How good are ‘AI doctors’ — and will they take over medicine?
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-01691-6

Nature talks to specialists about whether people might soon be diagnosed by artificial-intelligence systems.

item.title: White House proposes vast overhaul of US science funding: what you need to know
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-01779-z

The Trump administration’s proposal aims to improve transparency in federal funding, but critics fear the proposed rules would politicize research

item.title: Tiny hubs of metabolic activity optimize nitrogen use in maize
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-01583-9

Structures called plastoglobules organize the enzymes that turn nitrogen into compounds needed for plant growth, offering lessons for sustainable agriculture.

item.title: Nanostructure of tooth enamel casts light on dietary shifts as humans evolved
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-01579-5

The arrangement of mineral nanocrystals in the tooth enamel of primates, hominins and modern humans altered as the diet of these species changed.

item.title: Ubiquitin tags detected on non-protein biomolecules using new method
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-01741-z

An innovative method of mass spectrometry has detected the small protein ubiquitin on biomolecules other than proteins. In mouse liver, the energy-storing molecule glycogen has a large increase in ubiquitination — involving 1% of the liver’s total ubiquitin — during fasting, when glycogen is broken down.

item.title: Troubled waters: a plant protein senses when cells are running dry
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-01633-2

How cells sense fluctuations in the availability of water has long been unclear. The protein SAM8 is now shown to undergo a process called phase separation in a way that depends on its hydration, thereby sensing cellular water availability and linking changes in water status to the regulation of gene expression.

item.title: ‘Transformative’ CAR-T therapy allows three people to receive kidney transplants
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-01761-9

They had ‘highly sensitized’ immune systems that usually reject donated organs, leaving them with few options for survival.
